summary: A Dreamer tier no longer goes silently dead when one of its store calls hangs, and an objective that would make its tier silently inert now fails the gate instead.
details: The Dreamer runtime bounded only its model call, so a store read or write inside an adaptor that never returned left the loop holding that (adaptor, key) forever: the unit never ticked again and the only symptom was an absence. `inputs` and `commit` are now bounded at `[dreamer] store_timeout_seconds` (new, default 15s) times the adaptor's own declared store-call count, the unit is released, and the timeout gets its own reading on `nora_dream_store_timeout_total{adaptor,phase}` rather than being absorbed into the same `unavailable` a model outage produces. A collaborator's own timeout is deliberately not counted there.

The declared count lives in each adaptor's own module and is checked against that module's source, so a tier that grows a store call fails a test rather than quietly widening how long it may hold its own clock.

The proactive pass now stamps its daily clock at the END of its write sequence. Stamped first, a commit the new bound cancelled recorded the day as done with nothing written — and the reminders that pass had already created were orphaned, because the reconciliation that would have adopted them starts at that same clock.

Every shipped adaptor is now exercised by the adaptor contract suite, not one stand-in, and their items are driven through the real identifier screen in the order the runtime uses. Separately, each objective's own worked example is screened: an objective that shows the model a row id teaches it to return one, and every item it returns is then dropped before anything is written while the run still reports success. A tick where the screen rejects everything is counted on `nora_dream_empty_after_screen_total` in production.
limitations: The bound covers the adaptor's own `inputs` and `commit`. The loop's cursor reads around them — the watermark, the message batch, the schedule clock — are still unbounded; that is issue #191.

A `commit` cut off by the bound stops part-way through a tier's write sequence. The proactive pass and both note paths leave work the next tick re-selects; the note curator's discharge step, which is off by default, does not, and that is issue #195.

The bound releases the unit as soon as the phase can be cancelled. A collaborator that swallowed cancellation, or a synchronous blocking call, would still outlive it — nothing shipped does either today.
